title: Split slicer into its own repository
findings_note: owner: the split is what proves nothing project-specific is compiled in

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
slicer was written inside another project's working tree, where it was developed
against that project's real slice directory. That is why it works, and it is also why
it could not be published: the test fixture was a verbatim snapshot of that project's
review roadmap, and the README documented an install path that only made sense from the
parent directory.

Splitting it out is what makes the tool's central claim testable — that nothing in
`src/slicer/` hardcodes a path belonging to any one project. A repository that contains
no such project is the proof.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `tests/fixtures/legacy/` — replaced wholesale with a synthetic 14-slice tree
- `tests/test_import.py`, `tests/test_sync.py`, `tests/test_prose.py` — census numbers,
  pointer constants and pass keys follow the new fixture
- `README.md` — install path, the Tests section, a Status section
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` — new
- `LICENSE`, `.gitignore`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — new
- `pyproject.toml` — `[project.urls]`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
The suite is the test. Before the split it passed only because the fixture was real;
after it, the same 171 tests pass against a tree for a project that does not exist.

1. `test_Import_FixtureTree_RoundTripsEveryFileByteIdentical` — every file in the new
   fixture re-emits byte for byte, or the importer would refuse to migrate it.
2. `test_Import_FixtureTree_ReportsTheExpectedCensus` — 14 items, 4 passes, 5 groups,
   `S15` next.
3. `test_StatusLine_MigratedFixtureState_MatchesLegacyByteForByte` — the derived status
   line still reproduces its source exactly.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Author the replacement fixture to exercise what the old one did — a middot inside a
findings value, singular and plural tree keys, a collective trees cell, off-schema
headings, lead and note blocks, four passes, five phase groups, all four statuses, and
enough relative links to keep the link-rewrite invariant honest. Then follow the
failures: every number the tests assert about the old tree is a number about this one.

Keep `SLICER_LEGACY_TREE`. It is now the only way to prove the importer against real
hand-written markdown, and it keeps that proof private.

**Not in this slice:** publishing to PyPI, release tagging, and a second repository's
trial run — that is S02.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests   # 171 tests, OK
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check           # exit 0
```

And the one that matters for a public repository: no reference to the parent project
survives anywhere in the tree.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body:
One repository, `git@github.com:squalor-xyz/slicer.git`, public. The fixture
replacement lands before the first commit, because history is not a place you can take
something back out of.
